newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yeltsin clarifies nuclear missile statement.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin clarifies nuclear missile statement.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Tuesday that Russia would no longer target nuclear missiles at NATO states, clarifying an earlier remark in which he said the warheads would be removed from weapons aimed at NATO.

"The president means that the warheads will not be targeted at the states which have signed the (NATO-Russia) Founding Act," Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters after checking with Yeltsin on his impromptu comment at a NATO-Russia summit in Paris.

The spokesman said Yeltsin's statement, which took Western officials completely by surprise, had been a political goodwill gesture, although he stressed the Russian leader did envisage eventually dismantling the warheads.
"In future, the situation is possible when the warheads will be dismantled," Yastrzhembsky said.

Puzzled U.S. officials had said they would seek clarification of Yeltsin's initial remark to the summit that "everything that is aimed at countries present here, all of those weapons, are going to have their warheads removed".

The United States and Russia had previously agreed in arms control negotiations no longer to target each other's cities, but Yeltsin's decision appeared to go further and include the entire territory of the 16 NATO member states.
